title: ring144_24v, stride layout
claim: the study's starting point: the rotation pass laying riders out by stride. 546 batches of 1.6 contacts each is why it takes 520 ms.

marks.label: rigid rotation
marks.note: one loop_shift template turns the whole loop: every rider moves with one waveform. This is the broadcast primitive the ring is built around, and the reason it moves 72 ions per transport instruction.

marks.label: batch 1 of 546 / a 1-contact batch (292 of 546)
marks.note: a dock: 1 riders pull into their spurs at once. Each batch pays dock + undock + one forced cool (about 725 us) whatever its size; mean fill here is 1.6 contacts of 5 possible.  ALSO: one rider docks alone, and the batch still pays its full overhead: 292 such batches cost about 213.2 ms for 33.8% of the contacts. This is the 52%-fill headroom the taxonomy names.

marks.label: forced cool
marks.note: 300 us, once per batch: an ion that has crossed a junction carries 3 quanta against a 1-quantum gate budget, so the cool is structural, not a policy. It is about a quarter of the round.

marks.label: contact gates (1 pairs at once)
marks.note: the two-qubit gates of one batch, all in one instruction; each pair sits in its own dock. The Circuit pane shows which QASM statements this discharges.

marks.label: undock
marks.note: the riders leave their spurs. Entering the degree-3 rail node is charged as a junction crossing -- the price of the only mechanism a loop has.

marks.label: the fullest batch (5 contacts)
marks.note: every ancilla in use at once: this is what the lockstep placement is engineered to make happen, and the per-batch overhead is amortised best here.
